title: #thenotebook #broadway #musicaltheatre #ingridmichaelson #theatre
transcript: I saw the notebook musical, and I kinda loved it. For context, I've never read the book, and I only saw the movie one time, like seven years ago, and it didn't leave much of an impression on me. But this one. This one got me. I cried and I cried a lot. It might have resonated with me more just because I'm in a different phase of life. But also, I think it's partly because this story lent itself really well to being musicalized. And they actually took full advantage of that. And that's easier said than done. You know, the traditional format of, like, character breaks out into song to express a feeling. It's great. It's the foundation of the art form. But it's also very difficult to calibrate it correctly so that it's not interrupting the flow. And it doesn't seem like we're just telling a feeling instead of showing a feeling. But the notebook feels very tuned into that crucial wavelength. And it comes from a synergy between the direction of book music and lyrics. Although in this case, I think Ingrid Michaelson's lyrics are kind of the start of the show. There are a lot of lyrics that I loved, but one that has really stuck with me is when they sing, don't leave me now. Don't leave me then. Don't ever leave me again. And it's a straightforward lyric. It's not abstract, it's not subtext, but it hits on something profound. Especially the don't Leave me, then. Which is, like, inherently illogical, but that's the point. And I think a lot of musicals try to have that direct expression of a feeling, but they don't have the cutting emotional insight to back it up and to earn it. But I think the notebook does. I also love the use of three different actors to play the leads at different ages, where they work in conversation with each other, both in terms of how the show is structured, but also literally. They share the same space, they interact with each other sometimes or sing on each other's behalf. And this isn't new, right? Devices like this are actually pretty common in the theater. But first of all, I think the notebook does it extremely well. And secondly, I eat it up every time anyway, because I just think it's beautiful. And more specifically, the quintessential example of something that you can only really do properly in the theater as opposed to other mediums. And I love that, because theater has its own vocabulary and toolbox that allow you to do something really special if you know how to take advantage of them and aren't just trying to copy paste an IP onto a Broadway stage.
reasoning: Creator opens with 'I kinda loved it,' describes crying, praises the lyrics, direction, structure, and theatrical staging with genuine enthusiasm and no significant caveats.
